Corma Raises $125M Series A at $1B Valuation to Scale Defensive AI

Key Points Corma raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.

Corma raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.
Corma argues coding-focused models suit offensive security while defense needs continuous log and event analysis.
Compute capacity rather than model quality is Corma's immediate constraint on serving demand and its waitlist.
Defensive-cybersecurity company Corma announced on November 16, 2026 that it had raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation. NEA led the round, with continued participation from Sequoia Capital , Khosla Ventures and Coatue, bringing Corma’s total funding to $185 million.
Corma said the new capital would accelerate scaling of its foundation models, expand compute capacity and support selective hiring. The Series A follows its emergence from stealth on August 10, 2026 with $60 million in seed funding.
The company characterized demand from the world’s largest organizations as overwhelming and identified securing enough compute for that demand and its waitlist as one of its central challenges. Corma’s ability to expand access therefore depends on obtaining additional infrastructure as well as advancing its models.
How the Corma Workforce Operates
The company deploys those models through the Corma Workforce , a system designed to work autonomously alongside human security teams. It operates within customers’ existing security and IT stacks, including identity, cloud, endpoint, security information and event management, and firewall or intrusion-detection tools. Its work spans investigations, connecting evidence and taking action across those systems.
Employees can assign tasks through Slack or Teams, ask questions, review findings and approve actions. The design adds AI-led execution to a customer’s current operating environment while keeping human review in the workflow.
Corma reports live deployments across healthcare, finance, energy, critical infrastructure and retail, with 99% of security tasks completed autonomously and successfully, 100 times faster end-to-end completion and 95% lower cost per completed task.
One anonymized Fortune 1000 services-company CISO quoted on the product page said end-to-end response time fell 94% in a comparison with the customer’s former service provider, which the customer subsequently replaced with Corma.
Why Corma Uses Defense-Specific Models
Corma’s launch statement argues that improvements in coding and software reasoning map more directly to offensive security than to the broader defensive workload. Vulnerability research and exploit development are code-reasoning problems against bounded targets; defense instead requires continuous analysis of audit logs, events, configurations and network flows. It also involves connecting weak signals across systems and long periods while making thousands of accurate, consistent decisions each day under changing conditions.
That distinction is the basis for Corma’s focus on domain-specific foundation models. Its stated development program includes rethinking model architecture, extending context to detect faint anomaly signals, adversarial self-play and continuous learning that can establish baselines over months and years.

articles.title: Defensive AI agents co Corma raises $125m at $1b valuation - Globes
articles.snippet: Defensive AI agents co Corma raises $125m at $1b valuation Globes - Israel Business News
articles.text:
Israeli AI language model cybersecurity company Corma , today announced the completion of a $125 million Series A financing round, at a $1 billion valuation, led by NEA, alongside existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures. The company has now raised $185 million, having emerged from stealth just three months ago with a $60 million seed round led by Sequoia.
CEO Alon Pluda founded the company last year, after leaving Miggo Security, which he cofounded, following a dispute with his cofounders. Pluda is a graduate of the IDF Intelligence Corps’ prestigious Psagot program. He completed his service in 2022, following several years as a career officer in various technical roles at the core of Unit 8200’s technological operations. He founded Corma, which has 20 employees in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, with the aim of more effectively addressing AI-driven cyberattacks. The company achieves this by developing language models from scratch, rather than relying on existing models such as those from Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepSeek.
Pluda explains, "General-purpose language models are effective for tasks like software development or research and they are also excellent at identifying bugs and cyber vulnerabilities, which is precisely why hackers and attackers use them so efficiently. However, they are weak when it comes to defense. Defense requires a different kind of expertise: the ability to find a 'needle in a haystack' within the complex landscape of enterprise data systems, specifically regarding code and software maintenance, such as telemetry, logs, and events."
In Pluda’s view, this is why the language models currently on the market are highly advanced in their capacity to facilitate powerful cyberattacks, yet remain insufficiently developed for the purpose of defending organizations. Fluda explains that Corma addresses this gap by developing its own language model, which is focused entirely on a single task: perimeter defense for organizations. The company also develops AI agents that are integrated into client organizations, working alongside existing cybersecurity teams.
Pluda adds, "We don’t just provide CISOs with a dashboard or software to manage. We provide AI agents that empower them, enabling them to perform their jobs orders of magnitude better."
The company trains its models with the goal of achieving "superintelligence" for defensive cybersecurity - a capability that will allow security teams to operate at the speed and scale required to counter the advancement of AI-driven cyberattacks.
The company’s annual recurring revenue (ARR) is estimated to be in the tens of millions of dollars, and its client base includes companies from the Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 lists.
"Since its initial unveiling in August, demand for the company’s models has surged among organizations ranked in the Fortune 100, Fortune 500, and Fortune Global 500. To meet this demand, the company has increased its server capacity 24-fold," the company stated.
Corma works with large organizations, including companies in the healthcare, financial services, energy and critical infrastructure, retail, and telecommunications sectors. These organizations are increasingly delegating their security tasks to Corma’s autonomous workforce, which operates using a foundational model developed by the company.

Ameresco: $125 Million Financing From Nuveen With Expansion Capacity To $225 Million Supports European Energy Infrastructure Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:24 PM
Ameresco: $125 Million Financing From Nuveen With Expansion Capacity To $225 Million Supports European Energy Infrastructure Growth
Ameresco, an energy infrastructure company specializing in reliable power and infrastructure modernization, has secured a $125 million committed financing facility with Nuveen Energy Infrastructure Credit to support its expanding operations in the United Kingdom and Europe. The five-year revolving facility includes an option to increase financing capacity by an additional $100 million, potentially providing Ameresco with access to $225 million in total capital.
The facility matures in November 2031 and will provide dedicated financing for energy infrastructure projects and working capital requirements across Ameresco’s European business.
The financing has been structured with limited recourse to Ameresco and does not affect the company’s senior secured corporate leverage ratios.
This arrangement is intended to create a more self-sustaining capital structure for European operations while preserving financial flexibility at the parent-company level.
The facility will also allow Ameresco to expand available borrowing capacity as its project pipeline and working capital requirements increase, subject to the relevant terms.
The investment comes amid substantial growth in Ameresco’s European business.
European revenue increased from $62 million in 2022 to $529 million in 2025, representing more than an eightfold increase over that period.
The region now accounts for approximately 25% of Ameresco’s total revenue.
Ameresco attributes its European expansion partly to increasing electricity demand, higher energy costs, and growing customer interest in renewable energy infrastructure.
The company sees further opportunities in battery energy storage systems, commonly known as BESS, as European markets expand their use of technologies that can store electricity and provide greater flexibility to power networks.
Battery energy storage can help electricity customers manage demand fluctuations, integrate renewable generation, and strengthen energy resilience.
Ameresco believes its technology expertise and flexible approach to infrastructure development position it to support these requirements across European markets.
The company provides energy infrastructure solutions spanning behind-the-meter systems, utility-scale energy resources, and modernization of buildings and public infrastructure.
Its projects integrate multiple energy technologies according to customer needs rather than focusing on a single equipment or generation category.
Nuveen Energy Infrastructure Credit’s participation builds on an existing financing relationship with Ameresco.
The investment manager specializes in providing capital to companies and projects operating across energy infrastructure markets.
The new facility provides a dedicated financing source to support project execution without requiring Ameresco to rely exclusively on existing corporate financing arrangements.
Ameresco has delivered more than $15 billion in solutions and contracted over 5 gigawatts of energy resources since its founding in 2000.
Headquartered in Massachusetts, the company serves public and private sector customers throughout North America and Europe.

Altius Announces Estimated $122 Million TNR Gold Acquisition And Exploration Spinoff
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:23 PM
Altius Announces Estimated $122 Million TNR Gold Acquisition And Exploration Spinoff
Altius Minerals has agreed to acquire the TNR Gold shares it does not already own in a transaction with an estimated total value of $122 million, including shares in a newly formed exploration company.
The agreement will add royalty interests associated with Argentina’s Los Azules copper, Mariana lithium and Josemaria copper-gold projects.
Each eligible TNR share will be exchanged for 0.0072 Altius shares and 0.25 shares of TNR SpinCo. Based on November 10 prices and the assigned spinoff valuation, the implied consideration is approximately $0.48 per TNR share, representing a 60% premium.
That amount comprises approximately $97 million in Altius shares and $25 million in SpinCo shares.
SpinCo will hold the Shotgun Gold Project in Alaska and related assets and liabilities. Altius will retain a 0.5% net smelter return royalty on Shotgun.
Altius initially expects to own approximately 12% of SpinCo and will invest another $2.2 million to increase its stake to approximately 19.9%. It will also provide technical support.
The acquired royalties include an effective 0.36% net smelter return interest in Los Azules and an effective 1.35% interest in Mariana.
Los Azules is targeting a financing decision in mid-2027 and first production in 2030. Mariana has begun production and is ramping toward an initial target of 20,000 tonnes annually of lithium carbonate equivalent.
Shareholders controlling approximately 28% of TNR’s outstanding shares have signed support agreements.
Closing is expected around the first quarter of 2027, subject to shareholder, court, exchange and regulatory approvals. A shareholder meeting is expected in December 2026.
McCarthy Tétrault is serving as Altius’s legal counsel.
KEY QUOTES
“This transaction adds a significant development stage royalty over the Los Azules project, which offers the potential for decades of increased copper exposure within our portfolio. It also results in the consolidation of an operating stage royalty relating to the Mariana lithium brine project. Both of these assets feature attributes that are hallmarks of Altius’s long-term royalty investing strategy. With long to ultra-long potential resource lives, they provide growth optionality over multiple commodity cycles as well as projected cost curve positions that ensure long-term resiliency. We are also pleased to support the TNR SpinCo as it applies the historical project generation and royalty creation strategy that brought the Los Azules and Mariana royalties into its portfolio.”
Brian Dalton, CEO Of Altius Minerals
“The Arrangement Agreement with Altius is a pivotal milestone that fully validates the significant value we have created for TNR Gold shareholders. Altius is a premier and highly respected partner in the mining and royalty sector, and this Transaction delivers a compelling outcome for our shareholders, and we are thrilled to be making this announcement.”
Kirill Klip, Executive Chairman Of TNR Gold

Nvidia Backs Noeri’s $110 Million Enterprise AI Funding Round
Founded roughly five months ago by Stanford professors Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, the company is building AI tools tailored to businesses’ needs.
By John Kim
Published Nov 16, 2026, 11:17 AM EST
Save Share An unmarked accelerator board rests on a laboratory workbench / TokenPost.ai
Nvidia has joined a $110 million financing for Noeri, a five-month-old artificial intelligence startup building specialized systems for companies, adding another early-stage AI investment to the chipmaker’s portfolio.
Menlo Ventures was the lead investor. Madrona Venture Group, Kindred Ventures, NEA and Nvidia also participated. Noeri has not disclosed how much Nvidia invested, the startup’s valuation or how it plans to spend the funds.
Stanford professors Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin started Noeri roughly five months ago. The company focuses on adapting specialized AI systems to businesses’ needs using their proprietary data.
Nvidia has also participated in other AI startup financings. Its venture arm, NVentures, invested in Reactor , bringing that startup’s total funding to $74 million, and Nvidia participated in Simplismart’s $14 million Series B .

SA’s Yoco secures $100m credit facility to scale merchant cash advances
0
By
Tom Jackson
on
November 16, 2026
News , Southern Africa
South African fintech company Yoco has secured a US$100 million credit facility from US investment firm Victory Park Capital to expand its merchant cash advance operation.
Yoco builds tools and services to help small businesses accept card payments in-store and online, access loans, and manage their day to day activities. The startup has advanced more than ZAR6.5 billion (US$395 million) to over 40,000 merchants since 2018, working with specialist credit providers.
The company, which secured US$83 million in Series C funding back in 2021, has now secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital, which will allow it to scale its cash advance operations, and gain greater control over the pricing and risk of its merchant loans.
The aim is to use the transaction data generated by merchants using Yoco’s card machines and online payment tools to assess businesses that traditional lenders may struggle to evaluate, helping the company turn its payments relationship with more than 200,000 businesses into a larger cash advance operation.
“We have spent a decade building an operating system that runs a merchant’s whole business, payments, point of sale, and now the decisions in between. Financing was the one layer we didn’t fully control. This facility changes that,” said Yoco CEO Carsten Holtkemeyer.
Victory Park Capital brings experience in private credit and asset-backed finance to the arrangement, having invested more than US$12 billion across 260 investments since 2007. Senior partner Jason Brown, said Yoco had demonstrated a track record of supporting small and independent businesses.
“We’re supportive of Yoco’s mission to expand access to flexible financing solutions for South African entrepreneurs,” he said.

articles.text:
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:32 AM
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
Seawolf Therapeutics, a San Diego-based biotechnology company developing DNA-based medicines, has emerged from stealth with $100 million in funding and announced a multi-target research collaboration with Sanofi worth up to $1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, plus royalties. The company is developing a lipid nanoparticle-based DNA delivery platform designed to enable sustained production of therapeutic proteins inside patients’ cells.
Seawolf’s financing includes seed and Series A investments backed by Versant Ventures, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund, Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics, Sixty Degree Capital, Alexandria Venture Investments, and Pathway to Cures, the philanthropic venture arm of the National Bleeding Disorders Foundation.
Versant Ventures led the seed financing, while the Series A included Versant, MPM BioImpact, and Novartis Venture Fund.
The capital will support advancement of Seawolf’s proprietary therapeutic pipeline, including a lead program targeting metabolic diseases.
Developing The TRIDENT DNA Delivery Platform
Seawolf’s technology platform, called TRIDENT, stands for Targeted RNA-Induced DNA Expression via Nuclear Translocation.
The system uses lipid nanoparticles to transport DNA into cells and facilitate access to the nucleus, where genetic information can support production of therapeutic proteins.
Lipid nanoparticles are also used in certain RNA-based medicines, but RNA therapies can face limitations involving how long protein expression lasts.
Seawolf is developing a different approach intended to provide more durable protein production by delivering DNA-based payloads.
TRIDENT combines a proprietary lipid nanoparticle, DNA encoding a therapeutic protein, and an auxiliary factor that helps facilitate nuclear entry.
The company says its technology has demonstrated sustained protein expression above therapeutic levels in nonhuman primate studies at doses reported to be safe and well tolerated.
The company has also generated preclinical proof-of-concept results in animal models involving metabolic and rare diseases.
These findings remain preclinical and will require further evaluation before therapeutic benefits and safety can be established in humans.
A Redosable Approach To DNA Medicines
Seawolf is designing its technology to allow repeat administration when necessary.
The company describes TRIDENT as a nonviral DNA delivery approach that avoids some of the limitations associated with virus-based genetic medicine platforms.
Its goal is to provide durable protein expression while preserving the ability to adjust or supplement dosing.
The technology could support several therapeutic approaches, including replacement of defective genes and systemic production of biologic medicines.
Seawolf believes this flexibility may allow the platform to address multiple disease categories.
Sanofi Collaboration Includes Up To $1.2 Billion In Milestones
Alongside its funding announcement, Seawolf disclosed a multi-target research collaboration and exclusive license agreement with Sanofi.
The partnership will focus on developing undisclosed therapies for bleeding disorders and additional indications.
